title: BA1/2405/2021 of PREM LAL CHAMOLI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
First Bail Application No. 2405 of 2021
Prem Lal Chamoli ........Applicant

Present:-
Mr. Lokendra Dobhal, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. with Ms. Sonika Khulbe, Brief
Holder for the State.
Mr. Dinesh Chandra Joshi, Advocate for the informant.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 Applicant Prem Lal Chamoli is in judicial
custody in FIR No.13 of 2021, under Sections 354, 354-D,
504, 506, 376, 427 IPC, Section 3(1)(r)(s), Section 3(2)(v)
of The Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention
of Atrocities) Act, 1989 and Section 5/6 of the Protection
of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Police Station
Chamba, District- Tehri Garhwal. He has sought his
release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. FIR in the instant case was lodged on
18.05.2021 by the victim. According to her, in the month
of October, 2020, she used to join computer classes but

2
on her way to the computer class and back home, the
applicant would follow and molest her. On 16.03.2022, at
11:00, at night, the applicant smashed the door of the
victim's house. He used caste coloured remarks and also
threw a few articles in a field. According to the FIR, on
02.04.2021 also, the applicant attacked the father of the
victim.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would
submit that it is a case fit for bail; it is a false case; the
statement of the victim is not reliable; she has stated
about a rape on 02.01.2021, but it is not recorded in the
FIR. With regard to 16.03.2021 only, it is stated that the
applicant smashed the door; there is no witness to it; with
regard to the incident of 02.04.2021, there is no injury
report and the applicant is in custody for the offences not
related to it.
5. On the other hand, learned State Counsel
would submit that the victim has given categorical
description as to what had happened with her. She has
stated about the incident dated 02.01.2021, 16.03.2021
and 02.04.2021.

3
6. This is a stage of bail. Much of the discussion,
at this stage, is to be avoided, but to the extent of
appreciating the controversy, the material may be
examined with a caveat that any observation at this stage
shall have no bearing at the trial.
7. Fact remains that with regard to the incident of
02.01.2021, there is no mention in the FIR. On that date,
according to the victim, she was raped and in her
statement, at Para 19, she would say that on that date,
she had raised alarm. They are living only in two rooms.
She was in a room, which was bolted from inside when
the incident took place. She had called her parents. Did
not her family members intervene then? How did the
applicant ensure his entry into the room, which was
bolted from inside? Did the victim raise alarm for the first
time when the applicant ensured his entry in the room?
These and many more questions would definitely be
deliberated at the time of trial.
8. Having considered, this Court is of the view
that it is a case fit for bail and the applicant deserves to
be enlarged on bail.
9. The bail application is allowed.

4
10. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his
executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable
sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the
court concerned.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 14.10.2022
Ravi Bisht
